summary: Adaptive-batching rollout correlates with intermittent streaming freeze mid-response
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-10 22:00 UTC, FathomAI reports streaming chat sessions that pause mid-generation (no final newline or [DONE], SSE connection remains open but no chunks emitted for 10-60s), requiring client reconnects. Impact: customer production agent experiences degraded UX for long responses and elevated user drop rate. Environment: Hosted API (prod) region us-east-1, customer on Dedicated pool (redwood-ded-09).

Observed behavior:
- Streaming response begins normally and emits several token chunks, then stops emitting for tens of seconds while socket remains ESTABLISHED.
- Client-side shows no socket error; server shows request still attached to worker for a period then eventually request times out and returns 504 from api-gateway.

Expected behavior: continuous token chunks until model generation completes and final event delivered.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Create chat request with long system prompt + extended user context (~5k tokens).
2) Use SSE streaming endpoint with keepalive disabled on client.
3) Observe that after ~400-800 tokens, token emission halts without connection close.

Additional context: problem began after rollout of "adaptive-batching-v2" heuristic in serving-runtime on 2026-03-10 21:30 UTC. Similar reports from two other enterprise customers in us-east-1.

Relevant artifacts: traces, Grafana dashboards and logs referenced in investigation notes below.
comments: 2026-03-11 09:12 - Asha Patel (Support): Customer reports consistent mid-generation stalls for longer chat sessions after our recent adaptive-batching rollout. They provided sample request IDs: req-93a1f, req-93a6c, req-93b22.

2026-03-11 10:03 - Miguel Torres (SRE): Confirmed spike in 95/99th token latency for long seq lengths (~+220ms median tail) in grafana panel serving-runtime/tail-latency. Noting scheduling backpressure on ded-09 pool starting ~21:40 UTC. Investigating worker eviction traces.

2026-03-11 11:25 - Support (to customer): Asked for client keepalive configuration and whether they run proxies. Customer: TLS proxy with no SSE-specific keepalive. Advise: enabling client keepalive as temporary mitigation.

2026-03-12 01:18 - Miguel Torres (SRE): Correlated stalls with adaptive-batching-v2 path where worker enters an extended batching window for long contexts; KV-cache checkpointing combined with batch mixing causes intermittent head-of-line blocking. Created internal repro and linked PR to adjust batching thresholds.
2026-03-12 14:40 - Asha Patel (Support): Customer accepted workaround to rollback to earlier dedicated pool (redwood-ded-07) and enable client-side keepalive; requested timeline for permanent fix.

2026-03-13 08:10 - Miguel Torres (SRE): Deployed hotfix (serving-runtime PR 1124) that reduces max batch wait for long-context jobs and increases per-request liveness pings. Monitoring for improvement over 24h.
2026-03-13 13:02 - Support: Noted drop in reproductions after hotfix in us-east-1; customer to validate for next 48h before closure.
investigation_notes: Summary of findings: After rollback of adaptive-batching-v2 in a canary subset, observed disappearance of stalls. Root cause hypothesis: the new adaptive batching heuristic attempted to coalesce long-context requests into larger batches which inadvertently increased token inter-arrival variance. This created head-of-line blocking when a long context triggered KV-cache checkpointing/serialization on a worker, delaying emission of subsequent batched tokens for other requests attached to the same stream shard. Evidence: trace req-93a1f shows worker CPU spike and a 28s gap between last emitted chunk and subsequent processing; api-gateway logs show no connection close and no socket errors during gap. Metrics: 99th token latency for long-context requests increased from ~450ms to ~1.8s for the affected pool. Related system changes: adaptive-batching-v2 rolled out to 40% of workers in us-east-1 at 21:30 UTC on 2026-03-10 (deploy tag v20260310-adaptv2). We also observed a concurrent autoscaler tuning change that lowered eviction threshold which exacerbated worker churn. Next investigative steps taken: reproduced locally using long-context harness, instrumented per-request batching windows, added additional logging around KV-cache checkpoint events and batch flush timing. Linked PRs and canary telemetry attached above.
resolution: Immediate mitigation: rolled back adaptive-batching-v2 on affected dedicated pool (redwood-ded-09) and reverted autoscaler tuning for the pool. Hotfix deployed (serving-runtime PR 1124) to reduce max batch wait for long-context requests and to emit periodic liveness ping events for active streaming requests so API gateway can surface activity to clients. Customer workaround: move traffic to earlier pool redwood-ded-07 or enable client-side SSE keepalives (recommended interval 15s) until fix proves stable. Follow-ups: improve batching heuristics to avoid mixing long-context with short jobs (tracking task INT-3312), add e2e streaming regression tests for adaptive batching, and update rollout playbook to include streaming SLO smoke-tests. Monitoring: increased alerting on token inter-arrival gaps and added grafana dashboard panel for streaming-stall-rate. Pending customer confirmation for closure in 48h.
resolution_notes: Hotfix rolled out 2026-03-13 08:05 UTC to us-east-1 dedicated pools; post-deploy monitoring shows reduced stall incidence to near-zero for observed customers. Will keep ticket open until customer confirms stability.
public_notes: Customer-facing summary to include: We identified an interaction between a new batching heuristic and long-context jobs that could delay token emission for streaming responses. We've deployed a fix and provided a recommended workaround (client keepalive or pool switch) while we implement longer-term batching safeguards.
